news_drafts.headline: North Lanarkshire's housing revenue account gap for 2027/28 falls to £4.253m from £7.484m
news_drafts.lead:
North Lanarkshire Council's housing revenue account, the separate ring-fenced account for its own housing stock, paid for by rents, now has a budget gap of £4.253m for 2027/28. The medium-term financial plan presented in August 2026 put the gap at £7.484m. Revised planning assumptions reduced it by £3.231m, according to the paper going to the Housing Committee on 4 November 2026.

The paper sets cost pressures of £7.581m against base budget reductions of £3.328m, which leaves the £4.253m gap. It says the gap is to be reviewed at the December 2026 Council meeting, when estimates and rent levels for 2027/28 are to be approved.

Appendix 2 gives revised gaps for later years. For 2028/29 the gap is £9.751m, against £9.813m in the medium-term plan. For 2029/30 it is £13.998m, against £12.590m. The paper says unbudgeted pressures will be managed where possible through in-year action or unallocated reserves, with recurring impacts addressed in future medium-term financial plans.

news_drafts.headline: Strathclyde concessionary travel scheme shows £844k surplus for 2025/26, after £1.463m deficit a year earlier
news_drafts.lead:
The Strathclyde Concessionary Travel Scheme recorded a surplus of £844k on the provision of services in 2025/26, against a deficit of £1.463m in 2024/25. The figures are in a performance monitoring report on Strathclyde Partnership for Transport (SPT), the regional transport body, in the papers for North Lanarkshire's Environment and Climate Change Committee on 28 October.

Payments to operators fell from £5.451m in 2024/25 to £3.121m in 2025/26. The scheme's cost of services fell over the same period from £5.841m to £3.530m. Income from taxation and non-specific grants rose from £4.095m to £4.178m.

The report's table gives the 2025/26 result in brackets, which the table also uses for surpluses on other lines. It reads: "Deficit on provision of services 1,463 (844)". The figures are in thousands of pounds. The extract does not say why payments to operators were lower in 2025/26.

news_drafts.headline: North Lanarkshire health and social care board plan sets out £67.464m budget gap over three years
news_drafts.lead:
North Lanarkshire's Integration Joint Board (IJB), which oversees health and social care services delegated to it, has a medium-term financial plan (its plan for the next three years, showing the gap between what it expects to spend and what it expects to have). The plan identified a cumulative budget gap of £67.464m over the three years, including £23.923m in 2026/27. The approved budget for 2026/27 is £915.495m, and a recurring savings programme of £22.727m is measured against that year's gap.

The 2026/27 financial monitoring report shows social care services delegated to the partnership projecting an overspend of £4.872m before employee costs. Most of it relates to payments to other bodies, mainly care at home and independent care home places. Budgets were increased by £23.155m for inflation and expected demand, before a £7.900m savings requirement was applied. The paper links the overspend to demand, cost pressures and a shortfall against planned savings.

A separate reserves update, at period 6 (11 September 2026), gives a projected social care overspend of £1.647m. It assumes that sum will be funded from the Risk Reserve, money the board has set aside. It forecasts £5.008m of reserves used for social care. The board's governance progress paper says it approved a savings programme in March 2026 to meet the budget gap and that work on it is "well underway". It gives no savings amount.

findings.paper_title: Routes to Work Ltd – Performance & Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: The September 2026 update to the ALEO Review Action Plan records RTW03 on branding as complete.
findings.detail: The update says the new branding uses NLC's 'Work Here' identity and that contact with NLC Corporate Communications is ongoing where necessary. The plan has 13 actions, with other items recorded as ongoing or due by 31 March 2027.
findings.matters: A council finance director overseeing an ALEO review would want to see which recommendations are closed and which remain open.

findings.paper_title: Routes to Work Ltd – Performance & Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: The paper identifies a risk that Routes to Work and the wider employability programmes could be deemed non-compliant with external funders.
findings.detail: The paper says the company maintains a detailed risk register presented to each Board meeting. It does not describe the risk as having crystallised.
findings.matters: Non-compliance with external funders would put at risk the grant income the council and the company depend on.
findings.quote: the risk of Routes to Work and the wider employability programmes being deemed non-compliant with external funders is present.

findings.paper_title: Routes to Work Ltd – Performance & Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: Routes to Work reports targets met or exceeded in most 2025/26 employability indicators, with All Age Services starts and accredited qualifications shown as below target.
findings.detail: The paper reports All Age Services starts of 1175 against a full-year target of 1354, and accredited qualifications of 344 against 418, both shown as red. Job entries for the same service were 734 against 648.
findings.matters: A grant-funded programme running below its starts and qualification targets, while exceeding job outcome targets, is a mixed picture a funder would track.
findings.figures: All Age Services starts 1175 clients against 1354 target; accredited qualifications 344 against 418; job entries 734 against 648 target.
findings.quote: Performance is generally positive with targets being met or exceeded.

findings.paper_title: Routes to Work Ltd – Performance & Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: All-age services Q1 2026/27 starts reached 567 against a target of 186, including 310 clients transferred from the UK Shared Prosperity Fund programme that ended in March 2026.
findings.detail: The paper describes the transfer as an administrative exercise with no negative impact on service users. It says the high start figure is unusual for Q1.
findings.matters: A finance director would want to separate the funding-transfer effect from genuine new demand when reading starts against a target.
findings.figures: Clients engaging 567 against target 186; 310 clients transferred from UKSPF.

findings.paper_title: Routes to Work Ltd – Performance & Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: Q1 2026/27 out-of-work parents engaged stands at 127 against a target of 180, with the paper reporting a shortfall in parent engagement.
findings.detail: The paper says job outcomes for parents have still been met, and that steps were put in place after the issue was identified in July 2026. In-work parents engaged is 18 against a target of 31, also shown as red.
findings.matters: A shortfall in a funded engagement target is the kind of performance gap that may affect grant conditions and future funding.
findings.figures: Out-of-work parents engaged 127 against 180 target; in-work parents engaged 18 against 31 target.

daily_post.headline: Over £5m in grants were distributed to owners between 2020 and 2024, most of it for mandatory disabled adaptations.
daily_post.lead: Mandatory adaptation grants are a demand-led spend that councils and lenders can benchmark, since the volume depends on the age profile and disability levels of the local population.
